  lifecycle with the same rules as the desktop editor (lazy create,
  debounced writes, flush on leave, empty-note cleanup). Navigation is one
  native stack whose root is the menu screen (feed/folders tabs + sync/
  settings); Capture boots pushed on top of it, so the left-edge swipe-back

Done and pushed. Everything is on a new branch **`mobile-capture-gestures`** (two commits: a merge of latest `main` into the `home-pager` experiment, then the gesture rework). Typecheck and the mobile vitest suite pass; on-device feel is yours to judge — this VM can't run iOS.

**Branch question:** I built on the pager experiment, not main. The pager keeps Menu | Capture | Sync mounted side-by-side, which is the only clean way to get your #7 (returning to the same note with scroll intact — on main's push/pop stack the capture screen unmounts, and RN's TextInput can't restore scroll). It also hands all horizontal swiping to native paging physics, which un-crowds the gesture space for the vertical swipes. Your instinct about needing native code was half-right — `react-native-pager-view` *is* the native answer here, just without writing any ourselves.

How each complaint was addressed:

1. **Swipe-up with keyboard open** — works now; the gesture no longer cares about the keyboard, and since typing keeps you pinned to the bottom of the note, it's always armed right after typing.
2. **Hard to register** — the pan now uses manual activation driven by live (UI-thread) scroll geometry: it claims the touch after ~6px of upward pull at the bottom edge (instantly on short/empty notes), the page follows your finger 1:1 (was 0.4×), and on a long note one continuous drag scrolls to the end and rolls straight into filing — no lift-and-drag-again.
3. **Can't hide keyboard on scrollable notes** — scrolling moved to an outer ScrollView, so you get iOS-native `keyboardDismissMode="interactive"` (drag down toward the keyboard from anywhere, finger-tracking, Apple Notes style), plus a quick pull-down at the top still works.
4. **Scrollbar** — native indicator hidden (it's unstylable on a TextInput; that's what forced the ScrollView restructure). A custom 3px bar a few tints off the background (both themes) appears only while scrolling and fades out.
5. **Mic with content** — hidden the moment the page has text; tapping back in shows only the hamburger. It stays visible mid-dictation so you can stop it.
6. **Mic margin** — sits ~12px above the keyboard when it's open (was ~70px).
7. **Menu roundtrip** — pager pages stay mounted, so paging to the menu and back lands on the exact note, text, scroll and session untouched.

**The animation** is now the one you described: the current note slides up past the screen while a fresh canvas (same placeholder, hairline paper edge + soft shadow) rides in from below — from the keyboard's top edge while typing — and commits with a velocity-matched, non-bouncing spring. Two jank sources are gone by construction: the keyboard is never dismissed mid-flight (it stays up and you can keep typing on the new page), and the input isn't remounted (the swap happens while the incoming page fully covers the viewport).

**To test:** on your Mac, `git fetch && git switch mobile-capture-gestures`, `npm install`, then rebuild the dev client (`npx expo prebuild` + pod install) — pager-view is a new native dependency, so an old build won't do. TODO.md now carries the full on-device checklist.

One known trade-off of the new scroll architecture: caret-follow is handled for typing at the end (scroll anchoring, including while the keyboard animates in), but if you tap into the middle of a long note at the exact spot the keyboard then covers, the view won't auto-scroll to the caret anymore — a scroll fixes it. If that ever bothers you in practice, it's solvable with a small native caret-rect hook later.
